sealed.statement: Introduce sealed test-subsystem classification tooling for every live test, integrate subsystem freshness into repository workflow audits, and prove that the new classification has no authority over CI test selection.
sealed.title: seal subsystem classification tooling over every live test

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.
The subsystem manifest census must equal the primary and resource censuses exactly. A test may never be dropped, silently defaulted, or double-counted by classification.

Every subsystem value must be derived by a pure function of the test path from repository-declared state, never from timing, from filesystem contents outside the repository, or from manual per-test edits the deriver cannot reproduce.

This Quest adds classification and workflow freshness auditing only. No gate, shard, or manifest may change which tests CI selects; every pre-existing selection surface must stay byte-identical and no existing test may be reclassified on the primary or resource axes.

A test the deriver cannot classify, a rule matching nothing, and an override naming a dead path must each fail --check by name. Assigning an unmatched test to a catch-all subsystem is forbidden, because silent under-classification is indistinguishable from correct classification.

reason: Stage-1 subsystem classification is one atomic workflow/tooling change. Authored implementation is small and cohesive: 33768 of 434647 change bytes (7.8%) across four new files. The remaining 92.2% is canonical GENERATED state those files require - the 394180-byte subsystem census, the regenerated primary/resource manifests, the impact-graph seal, and the steering tools index that steering:check demands. These cannot be split into independently valid Quests: separating the generator from its generated census, or the freshness wiring from the manifest it checks, would deliberately create stale generated state and failing freshness gates. CI test selection is unchanged and independently demonstrated byte-identical on every existing shard file and gate manifest, with zero existing tests reclassified. Authorization applies only to this exact changed-path signature and this attempt.

hypothesis: Sealed subsystem classification tooling over all 2064 live tests across 22 subsystems. All-rules evaluation with 7 reasoned exact overrides and no catch-all; unclassified, ambiguous, dead-rule and dead-override cases each fail --check by name. Semantic digest covers path->subsystem, a separate evidenceDigest covers path->rule. Subsystem freshness wired into audit:shards. CI selection unchanged: every shard file and gate manifest byte-identical to baseline, no existing test reclassified.

claim: Model evidence report: the attempt's only model-flagged path (package.json) extended the audit:shards static gate with the subsystem-classification census check; no runtime model, statechart, TLA, architecture contract, decision table or invariant semantics changed. The contract produced by this Quest is the classification contract itself: test/shards/subsystem-classes.json, semantic digest fnv1a32-894af796 over path->subsystem with a separate evidenceDigest fnv1a32-acc85ea4 over path->rule, assigning all 2064 live tests exactly one of 22 semantic subsystems. It is verified fail-closed by the contract test (11 assertions) and by four mutation proofs: a removed rule reports unclassified by name, a duplicate rule reports ambiguous naming both rule ids, a rule matching nothing reports stale taxonomy, and an override naming a dead path reports a dead override. CI test selection is unchanged: every pre-existing shard file and gate manifest is byte-identical to 744c66271 and zero existing tests were reclassified on the primary or resource axes.
